clue.text: Son and wife of patriarch brought about trouble

indicators.note: brought about means turned round, so the son and wife pair is read backwards

parts.note: Sarah was the wife of the patriarch Abraham in Genesis

explanation.surface: A biblical family stirs up some unrest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought about' turns S + SARAH round as one piece; 'trouble' is a verb here, meaning to pester.
explanation.definitionFit: To trouble someone persistently is to pester or badger them.

clue.text: humble

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'humble (5)': only a definition survives, the wordplay is cut off and no scan or reprint gives it

clue.text: Gossip curtailed after trouble about unending impudence of stories

indicators.note: after places the shortened gossip word behind the rest
about means surrounding, so the word for trouble wraps round the next piece

parts.note: ado is fuss or trouble

indicators.note: unending means the last letter of the word for impudence is dropped

parts.note: neck is British slang for cheek or nerve, as in 'brass neck'

indicators.note: curtailed means docked of its tail, so the final letter goes

parts.note: talk is gossip

explanation.surface: Idle chatter gets cut short by a fuss over someone's cheek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gossip' looks like the definition but is wordplay; 'of stories' defines. NECK for cheek is British slang ('brass neck'), and 'unending' and 'curtailed' each drop a final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Anecdotal means relating to or consisting of short personal accounts or tales.

clue.text: Quiet and interested in religion

parts.note: sh is the call for silence
to be into something is to be keen on it

explanation.surface: Someone calm and curious about faith.
explanation.definitionFit: Shinto is the native faith of Japan, venerating kami spirits.

clue.text: Agent in time receiving European support

indicators.note: receiving means taking in, so the word for time holds the other pieces

parts.note: a date is a point in time
a leg is a support, as of a table

explanation.surface: An operative serving out their time with help from Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: A delegate is a representative sent to act on behalf of others.

clue.text: Course, with greens, designed to have powerful effect?

definitions.text: Course, with greens, designed to have powerful effect?

parts.words: Course, with greens, designed to have powerful effect
parts.note: reads like a golf course or a meal with vegetables, but 'course' is a policy and 'greens' are greenbacks, US banknotes, used to gain influence abroad

explanation.surface: A golf course or a meal with greens built to make a strong impression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greens' are US dollar bills (greenbacks); the phrase means foreign policy that wins influence through money rather than force.
explanation.definitionFit: The term describes a foreign policy of using financial investment and loans to extend a nation's influence.

clue.text: Certainly involved in a lot of work, with little time to be idler

indicators.note: involved in means set inside, so the word for certainly goes into the shortened work word
a lot of means most of, so the final letter of the work word is dropped

parts.note: labour is work
ay (aye) is an old way of saying yes, certainly
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Someone who is surely busy with plenty of work finds little time to loaf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Certainly' gives the old affirmative AY; 'a lot of' drops the last letter of the work word, and 'involved in' sets AY inside what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: A layabout is a lazy person who avoids work, a loafer.

clue.text: Rising star for example has class

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means read from bottom to top, so both pieces are turned round together

parts.note: the sun is a star

explanation.surface: An up-and-coming celebrity turns out to be classy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' turns SUN + EG as a whole, giving GE + NUS.
explanation.definitionFit: In biological classification a genus is a rank grouping related species, a kind or category.

clue.text: Interest? Develop it a little

indicators.note: develop means work up into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Arouse curiosity, then expand on the idea a bit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Develop' rearranges the nine letters of IT A LITTLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To titillate is to excite or stimulate pleasurably, to arouse curiosity.

clue.text: One in meeting backing friend to a significant extent

indicators.note: backing means supporting from behind, so the meeting piece goes after the friend

parts.note: a mate is a friend

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the one goes into the meeting word

parts.note: a rally is a mass meeting
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone at a rally supports a pal in a big way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One in meeting' gives RIALLY, which stands behind MATE, as 'backing' says.
explanation.definitionFit: Materially means substantially or considerably, in a way that matters.

clue.text: Gain skill without end in practice area

parts.note: to net is to gain as profit

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the word for end is taken out of skill

parts.note: to kill is to end

explanation.surface: Improve one's game in the practice ground.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing KILL (end) from SKILL leaves S. Nets are the netted pitches where cricketers practise batting and bowling.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, nets are enclosed practice pitches surrounded by netting.

clue.text: Quarrel with old soldier about objective required by army

indicators.note: about means around, so the old soldier wraps round the objective

parts.note: vet is short for veteran, an old soldier
an end is an aim or objective
TA is the Territorial Army, the British volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: A veteran argues over the goals the army wants.
explanation.walkthrough: The TA (Territorial Army) is the British army's part-time reserve force.
explanation.definitionFit: A vendetta is a long bitter feud between parties.

clue.text: Two characters changing places in cunning activity

indicators.note: two letters swap positions within the word for cunning

parts.note: subtle means crafty or cunning

explanation.surface: Two people swap roles in a sly operation.
explanation.walkthrough: The S and B of SUBTLE swap places, giving BUSTLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Bustle is busy, energetic movement and commotion.

clue.text: Recognise moral flaw

definitions.meaning: to pick out or notice something
a stain on one's character or reputation

explanation.definitionFit: To notice is to pick out, and a blemish on character is a stain, both senses of the one word.

clue.text: Tending to initiate change, top vicar worked with energy

indicators.note: worked means shaped or kneaded, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A senior clergyman toils energetically, always pushing for reform.
explanation.definitionFit: Being proactive means acting in advance to cause events rather than reacting to them.

clue.text: Expression of annoyance about most of colour in tattoo?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the exclamation goes round the colour

parts.note: drat is a mild curse

indicators.note: most of means all but the last letter

parts.note: umber is a brown earth colour

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles about the shade of ink in a tattoo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tattoo' looks like body art; here it is a drum signal, as in a military tattoo.
explanation.definitionFit: A tattoo is a rhythmic signal beaten on a drum, originally recalling soldiers to quarters.

clue.text: Amount of pressure on sensitive person serving in pub

parts.note: a bar is a unit of pressure
tender means sore or sensitive

explanation.surface: A thin-skinned person under pressure works behind the counter.
explanation.definitionFit: A bartender mixes and serves drinks behind the counter of a bar.

clue.text: Part of shoe with slit showing sock

parts.note: the upper is the part of a shoe above the sole
a cut is a slit

explanation.surface: A slit shoe exposes the wearer's sock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sock' is not hosiery but a punch.
explanation.definitionFit: Sock is slang for a hard blow, and this is an upward punch to the chin.

clue.text: Sweet little ball, in table game, rolling around

indicators.note: rolling around means turning over, so the whole assembly is read backwards
in means placed inside, so the little ball goes into the table game

parts.note: pool is a game played on a cue table
a pill is a small ball

explanation.surface: A small ball rolls about a pool table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet' is a noun here, a confection; 'rolling around' turns the whole ball-in-game assembly back to front, not just the table game.
explanation.definitionFit: A lollipop is a boiled sweet on a stick.

clue.text: Felt sorry for being offensive in speech

indicators.note: in speech means as spoken, so the word for offensive is heard rather than written

parts.note: rude means offensive

explanation.surface: Someone regrets being insulting in what they said.
explanation.definitionFit: To rue something is to regret it bitterly.

clue.text: Food taken aboard ship in large quantities

indicators.note: taken aboard means put inside the vessel, so the food goes into the ship

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
tack is food, especially hard ship's biscuit

explanation.surface: Provisions loaded onto a vessel in bulk.
explanation.definitionFit: Stacks is informal for a great amount, as in 'stacks of money'.

clue.text: Uncommon heart of batsman, with century, in charge

indicators.note: heart of means the middle letter of the word
in means inside, so the century goes into the charge word

parts.note: care is charge, as in 'in someone's care'
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A rare innings in which a batsman scores a hundred while in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle letter of BATSMAN is S; C inside CARE gives CARCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarce means in short supply, rare.

clue.text: Sailor getting up after drink for dance

indicators.note: after places the sailor behind the drink

parts.note: rum is a drink

indicators.note: getting up in a down clue means rising, so the letters are read upwards

parts.note: AB is an able seaman

explanation.surface: A sailor rises after a drink to dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The rumba is a ballroom dance of Cuban origin.

clue.text: Love shown by one in Dutch city, endlessly making effort to improve social welfare

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

indicators.note: in means inside, so the one goes into the shortened city
endlessly means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: Utrecht is a city in the Netherlands
a means one

explanation.surface: Charity shown by someone in a Dutch city working tirelessly for social good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' trims UTRECHT to UTRECH, and A goes in to give UTREACH.
explanation.definitionFit: Outreach is the work of extending services or help to people in the community.

clue.text: Preserve acceptable Church decree

parts.note: to can food is to preserve it
on means acceptable, as in 'that's not on'

explanation.surface: Keep up an approved ruling of the Church.
explanation.definitionFit: A canon is a law or rule laid down by a church council.

clue.text: Stable made of wood by Mike

parts.note: fir is a softwood timber
Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A sturdy structure made of timber by a man called Mike.
explanation.definitionFit: Firm means solid, steady and secure.

clue.text: Companion, once gemstone

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Companion, once gemstone (10)': no wordplay gives the ten letters from these words; the clue seems cut short and no scan or reprint gives the rest

clue.text: Tendency to quibble with exercises and, after revision, with test

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercises

indicators.note: after revision means rearranged, so the letters of and are reordered

parts.note: to try is to test

explanation.surface: A nitpicker reviews physical exercises and a test.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after revision' rearranges the word 'and' to sit between the exercises and the test; the definition is the opening phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedantry is excessive concern with minor details and rules.

clue.text: Hardy's rank?

definitions.meaning: rank means pungent, having a powerful smell

explanation.definitionFit: Robust and pungent are both senses of the one adjective describing great force or intensity.
